of Psychiatry &middot; [presented]{.status .done}\
Bekdemir F, Özdin S, Satılmış B, Aydın Öztemel R, Bolat R, Ünsal Çelebi D
&middot; [doi:10.5080/kes27.abs62](https://doi.org/10.5080/kes27.abs62)

:::

Gambling disorder is usually treated as one behavioural category. This study
looked at three things together in the same patients — personality traits,
impulsivity, and the beliefs people hold about gambling itself — to ask
whether the psychology behind the disorder differs by who is affected and by
how early the problem started.

Participants were adults in treatment at the Ondokuz Mayıs University
psychiatry outpatient clinic and at AMATEM in Samsun, diagnosed by DSM-5
criteria. Severity was measured with the South Oaks Gambling Screen,
cognitive distortions with the Gambling-Related Cognitions Scale, impulsivity
with the Barratt Impulsiveness Scale short form, and personality with the
Eysenck Personality Inventory, alongside PHQ-9 and GAD-7.

::: {.k}
findings are in the published abstract; the record above is authoritative
:::

This work sits apart from the computational thread running through the rest of
this page — it came out of clinical service rather than out of the modelling
programme, and shares neither its method nor its question.
